concerns.analysis: Several meaningful charts that appear in the source document are completely missing from the rendered HTML output. Instead of rendering the images, the HTML pipeline output an HTML comment indicating the images are missing data.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Page 24 contains Figure 7, a bar chart titled 'How important is smoothing to your business needs?'
concerns.output_quote: The chart image is missing and replaced by an HTML comment: '<!-- image without data: A bar chart titled 'How important is smoothing to your business needs?'... -->'
concerns.location: Page 24 (and similarly on pages 34, 35, and 38 for other charts)

concerns.analysis: On page 40, the source PDF contains a single image showing both a bar chart and its corresponding data table. In the HTML output, the image containing the table is displayed, and the table data is transcribed again as a separate HTML table element immediately below it, resulting in the data being shown to the user twice.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Page 40 contains an image of a bar chart integrated with a data table showing survey responses ('Extremely important', 'Very important', etc.).
concerns.output_quote: The HTML includes both the full image containing the data table and a separate `<table>` element transcribing the same data below it.

concerns.description: Table caption coded as header row: 7 table(s) have a single spanning first row that is likely a caption/title
concerns.analysis: caption_as_header=7. Examples: p12: "ATLAS_Hydrography_v2 feature table"; p13: "ATLAS FEATURETYPE Domain"; p13: "ATLAS HYDROTYPE Domain". First row spans all columns — should be a <caption> element, not a header row.

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 4 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=4, examples=['3D National Terrain Model (3DNTM,)', 'Elevation-Derived Hydrography Acquisition Specifications', 'Representation, Extraction, Attribution, and Delineation']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

The source document underlines the word 'Recommendation:' in several places throughout the document to provide emphasis. In multiple instances (e.g., page 23), this underline is lost in the output, which relies only on bold/italics without capturing the underline.
concerns.output_quote: ***Recommendation:*** ***Combine segments between confluences. Reaches will be split where needed to represent breaks in DWR Assessment Units.***

concerns.description: Degenerate images detected: 68 images with extreme aspect ratio or tiny dimensions

concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=43. Header/footer elements are present in extraction data. This is common in multi-page government PDFs and is typically cosmetic — the renderer strips them from HTML output.
